long_biography.plain_text:
Holekamp joined Enterprise's parent company in St. Louis in 1976 after earlier work at its rental-car business. Four years later, he moved to California to acquire and revive a struggling rental operation, earning compensation tied to profits. He later returned to St. Louis as Enterprise executive vice president and retired at the end of 2000.

A stock award tied to Holekamp's senior role gave him an equity interest in the parent company, which was later redeemed after a valuation dispute. He then shifted toward investment and stewardship through Holekamp Capital and as a founding partner of Alitus Partners, a long-horizon investor in small businesses. Holekamp has also funded university entrepreneurship programmes and served institutions including the Barnes-Jewish Hospital Foundation, the Saint Louis Science Center and The Muny.
